description:
One challenging situation I faced was making a search component fully accessible. At that time, I wasn't very familiar with accessibility, especially VoiceOver behavior.

The component had dynamic suggestions, keyboard navigation, search and multi-select options, so making it accessible wasn't simple. I first spent time to understand the basics how screen readers work and how focus should move between elements. I also connected with the accessibility team to clarify the expected behavior.

Then I updated the component by adding proper ARIA attributes, fixing the tab order, and making sure focus moved correctly between the input and dropdown options. After that, I tested component to ensure everything was announced correctly and could be used with/without a mouse.

At end, the component passed accessibility checks, and It also helped me gain practical knowledge in accessibility hands-on experience with accessibility, which I later applied to other components.

subtopic: Taking Over DMS Project Leadership Close to Production
description:
One major challenge I faced was during the DMS project when there was no proper technical lead handling the application, and ownership was moved to me close to production deployment with only around 1 to 1.5 months left. The application was in a very unstable state, and many modules were not functioning correctly.

Initially, we assumed most issues were from the frontend side and that backend APIs were stable. I took ownership of grooming stories, planning the work, prioritizing critical flows, and coordinating the team to rewrite major parts of the frontend application along with new feature implementation.

We were able to stabilize the UI and prepare the application with only minor bugs remaining. However, during final workflows like shipment submission and reassignment, we discovered major backend API issues that were impacting core functionality and delaying production delivery.

The biggest challenge was communicating these unexpected dependencies and delays to stakeholders while coordinating multiple teams under tight timelines. From this experience, I learned the importance of early end-to-end integration validation, dependency tracking, and proactive risk communication instead of assuming downstream systems are stable.
key_points: Took ownership of unstable DMS project 1-1.5 months before production
Planned work, prioritized critical flows, and coordinated UI stabilization
Discovered major backend API issues during final workflow testing
Challenging to communicate delays and coordinate teams under tight deadlines
Learned the importance of early end-to-end integration validation and dependency tracking
Learned proactive risk communication instead of assuming downstream stability
